issue.title: Run CodeQL from a workflow instead of default setup

labels.name: decision: accepted
labels.description: An owner accepted this decision, so T3 pull requests may proceed

issue.body: ### Problem statement CodeQL runs under default setup, which takes no path or concurrency options. Every pull request push gets the Actions, JavaScript and Python analyses, whatever it changed. In the runs I sampled on 2026-10-08 the JavaScript job averaged 267s on pull requests, Python 60s and Actions 46s, about 373s of runner time per run against 343s for the whole Code Quality workflow. A docs-only pull request pays for all of it. ### Proposed solution Replace default setup with `.github/workflows/codeql.yaml` (#9187): - Same three languages, default query suite and `/language:` categories, so existing alerts carry over. - Pull requests that only touch Markdown or MDX skip the workflow, and each language job skips its analysis when the pull request does not touch that language. - Pushes to `main` and a weekly schedule always analyze everything. This needs a decision because the workflow grants `security-events: write` to its analyze job, and because default setup has to be turned off in the repository settings just before the pull request merges. Between those two steps nothing else changes: CodeQL is not a required check and no ruleset has a code scanning rule. ### Alternatives considered - Keep default setup. No path filter is available, so the cost stays. - Workflow-level `paths-ignore` only. It skips docs-only pull requests but still runs Python and Actions analyses on the roughly 9 in 10 pull requests that touch neither.

issue.title: Stop caching the pnpm store on GitHub-hosted runners

labels.name: decision: accepted
labels.description: An owner accepted this decision, so T3 pull requests may proceed

issue.body: ### Problem statement Seven workflows on `ubuntu-latest` cache the pnpm store. The cache makes those jobs slower, and it takes up a large share of the repository's Actions cache storage. **It costs more time than it saves.** One copy of the store is a 1.5 GB archive. Restoring it takes 25 to 47 seconds, and the install that follows is barely faster than downloading from the registry. Setup plus install on 2026-10-09: | Job | Store cache | Setup | Install | Post step | Run | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | Test Coverage | on | 45s | 28s | 0s | [job](https://github.com/assistant-ui/assistant-ui/actions/runs/37952245933/job/113893906006) | | Test Coverage | on | 41s | 21s | 11s | [job](https://github.com/assistant-ui/assistant-ui/actions/runs/37951798632/job/113892176278) | | Test Coverage | off | 3s | 27s | 0s | [job](https://github.com/assistant-ui/assistant-ui/actions/runs/37953401080/job/113897700291) | | VS Code Test Bed | on | 39s | 20s | 12s | [job](https://github.com/assistant-ui/assistant-ui/actions/runs/37951798837/job/113892177124) | | VS Code Test Bed | off | 3s | 26s | 0s | [job](https://github.com/assistant-ui/assistant-ui/actions/runs/37953401100/job/113897700573) | | Changesets | on | 34s | 10s | 21s | [job](https://github.com/assistant-ui/assistant-ui/actions/runs/37951798841/job/113892182460) | | Changesets | on | 26s | 9s | 0s | [job](https://github.com/assistant-ui/assistant-ui/actions/runs/37936235782/job/113838882684) | | Deploy Examples (with-expo) | on | 36s | 23s | 17s | [job](https://github.com/assistant-ui/assistant-ui/actions/runs/37951798774/job/113892276598) | | Deploy Examples (with-react-ink-web) | off | 3s | 11s | 0s | [job](https://github.com/assistant-ui/assistant-ui/actions/runs/37951798774/job/113892276428) | The "off" rows for Test Coverage and VS Code Test Bed are from #9184. In the logs, the cached jobs report `Cache Size: ~1445 MB (1514955331 B)` and then `resolved 2832, reused 2832, downloaded 0`. The uncached jobs report `reused 0, downloaded 2686` and finish the install in about the same time. A non-zero post step is the job uploading a new copy after the lockfile changed. These are not one-off runs. Across every successful job between 11:53 and 16:38 UTC on 2026-10-08, from the Actions jobs API: | Job | Store cache | Jobs | Setup, median (range) | Install, median (range) | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | Test Coverage | on | 24 | 43s (25-57s) | 22s (19-35s) | | Changesets | on | 7 | 38s (27-110s) | 9s (8-9s) | | VS Code Test Bed (Probes) | on | 4 | 30s (25-31s) | 20s (19-22s) | | Build Changed Packages | off | 30 | 3s (2-5s) | 22s (14-32s) | | Build Changed Apps (Blacksmith) | on | 29 | 14s (11-33s) | 3s (2-13s) | Changesets is the worst case. It installs 898 packages with a filter ([`changeset.yaml#L37`](https://github.com/assistant-ui/assistant-ui/blob/4ec2945e53f67f01b35dc0395df1f91c0b9f5cf4/.github/workflows/changeset.yaml#L37)) but restores the whole store first, on every push to `main`. The 110s setup in the table is [one slow restore](https://github.com/assistant-ui/assistant-ui/actions/runs/37787559373/job/113346123624). **It fills the cache allowance.** `pnpm/setup` ends the cache key with the lockfile hash ([`keys.ts#L13-L19`](https://github.com/pnpm/setup/blob/703c52620218391530e48b9e8870d5c0082e1b9b/src/cache-restore/keys.ts#L13-L19)) and saves a new copy whenever the restored key is not an exact match ([`cache-save/run.ts#L20-L25`](https://github.com/pnpm/setup/blob/703c52620218391530e48b9e8870d5c0082e1b9b/src/cache-save/run.ts#L20-L25)). Every lockfile change on `main` therefore adds about 1.5 GB, and a pull request that changes the lockfile adds its own copy. Cache usage on 2026-10-09, from `gh api repos/assistant-ui/assistant-ui/actions/cache/usage` and the [cache list](https://github.com/assistant-ui/assistant-ui/actions/caches): | Time (UTC) | Total | Store copies | | --- | --- | --- | | between 15:09 and 15:28 | 11,860,906,549 bytes (11.86 GB) | 3, about 4.55 GB | | 15:59 | 10,216,307,124 bytes (10.22 GB) | 4, 6.06 GB | GitHub's default limit is 10 GB per repository, and the first reading is over it however it is counted. Past the limit, GitHub evicts the least recently used caches, and its docs name "removing caching from specific workflows" as a fix for the churn this causes ([usage limits and eviction policy](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/workflows-and-actions/dependency-caching#usage-limits-and-eviction-policy)). That is what happened between the two readings: five CodeQL caches were evicted while a fourth store copy was saved. ### Proposed solution Set `cache: false` on the `pnpm/setup` step in `test-coverage.yaml`, `changeset.yaml`, `vscode-test-bed.yaml`, `react18-weekly.yaml`, `pkg-pr-new.yaml`, `registry.yaml` and `deploy-examples.yaml`. #9184 does this. Build Changed Apps keeps its cache. It runs on Blacksmith, where the restore is fast enough to pay off. Every other job already has the cache off, including Build Changed Packages and the publish workflows. Those leave it off for a different reason, which also fits here: "hardened against cache poisoning for sensitive publish operations" ([`npm-publish.yaml#L697`](https://github.com/assistant-ui/assistant-ui/blob/4ec2945e53f67f01b35dc0395df1f91c0b9f5cf4/.github/workflows/npm-publish.yaml#L697), [`pypi-publish.yaml#L250`](https://github.com/assistant-ui/assistant-ui/blob/4ec2945e53f67f01b35dc0395df1f91c0b9f5cf4/.github/workflows/pypi-publish.yaml#L250)). Changesets runs with `contents: write`. The small lockfile verification cache is unaffected. `pnpm/setup` restores it whether or not the store is cached ([`cache-restore/run.ts#L34-L40`](https://github.com/pnpm/setup/blob/703c52620218391530e48b9e8870d5c0082e1b9b/src/cache-restore/run.ts#L34-L40)). `changeset.yaml` is a decision path in [`.github/review-policy.json#L57`](https://github.com/assistant-ui/assistant-ui/blob/4ec2945e53f67f01b35dc0395df1f91c0b9f5cf4/.github/review-policy.json#L57), so the pull request is T3 and needs this decision before it can merge. ### What it costs - Every one of these jobs downloads its packages from the npm registry on each run. A registry outage or a slow day would hit them directly. Build Changed Packages and the other uncached jobs already work this way. - The Changesets number is an estimate. The workflow only runs on `main`, so it cannot be measured before merge. The closest comparison is the with-react-ink-web deploy, which installs 1,183 packages uncached in 3s + 11s. - `pkg-pr-new.yaml`, `react18-weekly.yaml` and `registry.yaml` run too rarely to measure on the pull request. They use the same full install as Test Coverage. ### Alternatives considered - **Leave Changesets cached and change the other six.** That keeps the pull request at T2. Changesets would then be the only job reading the cache and the only one writing it, so it would keep restoring 1.5 GB to install 898 packages and uploading a new copy on every lockfile change. - **Raise the cache limit.** Storage past 10 GB is billed, and it does nothing about the restore time. - **Move these jobs to Blacksmith.** That is a larger change with its own cost, and most of these jobs are short. ### Rollout 1. Merge #9184. 2. The existing store copies stop being read. GitHub removes caches that have not been accessed in 7 days, or a maintainer can delete them from the caches page. 3. Check setup and install on the first Changesets run on `main`. If it is slower than before, reverting is one line in that file. ### Decision needed Should the pnpm store cache be turned off on GitHub-hosted runners, including in `changeset.yaml`? If yes, an owner of the CI and policy area labels this issue `decision: accepted`.

+# @assistant-ui/vscode
+
+Run [assistant-ui](https://www.assistant-ui.com/) inside a VS Code extension webview.
+
+See the [VS Code guide](https://www.assistant-ui.com/docs/guides/vscode) for the architecture, a quick start with `npx assistant-ui create -t vscode`, and the limitations of webviews.
+
+A webview cannot reach your backend with `fetch`, so this package tunnels `fetch` over the webview's `postMessage` channel. Your route handlers (`(req: Request) => Response`) run unchanged in the extension host, and their responses stream back to the webview.
+
+## Entry points
+
+- `@assistant-ui/vscode/host` runs in the extension host. It never imports the `vscode` module.
+- `@assistant-ui/vscode/webview` runs in the webview bundle.
+
+## Extension host
+
+```ts
+import { serveWebviewRoutes } from "@assistant-ui/vscode/host";
+import { POST } from "./api/chat";
+
+export function resolveWebviewView(view: vscode.WebviewView) {
+  view.webview.options = { enableScripts: true };
+  const server = serveWebviewRoutes(view.webview, {
+    "/api/chat": { POST },
+  });
+  view.onDidDispose(() => server.dispose());
+}
+```
+
+Unknown paths answer `404`, unsupported methods `405`, and a handler that throws `500`. Aborting the request in the webview aborts `req.signal` in the handler. `serveWebviewRoutes` serves routes only: host calls from `installLinkInterceptor` or `createVSCodeStorage` reject in the webview, so use [`serveWebviewHost`](#host-services) when the webview uses them.
+
+## Webview
+
+Pass `vscodeFetch` to any runtime that takes a `fetch`:
+
+```tsx
+import { useChatRuntime, AssistantChatTransport } from "@assistant-ui/react-ai-sdk";
+import { vscodeFetch } from "@assistant-ui/vscode/webview";
+
+const runtime = useChatRuntime({
+  transport: new AssistantChatTransport({ api: "/api/chat", fetch: vscodeFetch }),
+});
+```
+
+## Host services
+
+`serveWebviewHost` serves the same `routes` as `serveWebviewRoutes` and also answers the webview's calls into the host. Use it in place of `serveWebviewRoutes`:
+
+```ts
+import { serveWebviewHost } from "@assistant-ui/vscode/host";
+
+const host = serveWebviewHost(view.webview, {
+  routes: { "/api/chat": { POST } },
+  openExternal: (url) => vscode.env.openExternal(vscode.Uri.parse(url)),
+  storage: context.globalState,
+});
+view.onDidDispose(() => host.dispose());
+```
+
+### External links
+
+A webview cannot navigate away or open windows. `installLinkInterceptor()` catches clicks on absolute `http:`, `https:`, and `mailto:` links, plus `window.open` calls, and asks the host to open them with `openExternal`. The host checks the scheme again against `externalSchemes` before calling it. Relative links, `#anchors`, and clicks the app already `preventDefault`ed are left alone.
+
+```ts
+import { installLinkInterceptor } from "@assistant-ui/vscode/webview";
+
+installLinkInterceptor();
+```
+
+### Thread persistence
+
+`createVSCodeStorage()` stores threads in the Memento passed as `storage` (`context.globalState` or `context.workspaceState`), so they survive reloading the window. Its keys are namespaced by `storagePrefix` (default `"@assistant-ui/vscode:"`).
+
+```tsx
+import { createLocalStorageAdapter } from "@assistant-ui/core/react";
+import { useRemoteThreadListRuntime } from "@assistant-ui/react";
+import { AssistantChatTransport, useChatRuntime } from "@assistant-ui/react-ai-sdk";

issue.title: Require Test Coverage and run it in the merge queue

labels.name: decision: accepted
labels.description: An owner accepted this decision, so T3 pull requests may proceed

issue.body: ### Problem statement A pull request with failing tests can queue and merge. The rulesets require `autofix`, `Build Changed Packages`, `Typecheck Changed Packages`, `Review Policy Scripts` and `review-tier`, and none of those runs a test. Test Coverage is the only workflow that does, and it is neither a required check nor triggered for merge groups. In the 1000 workflow runs I sampled on 2026-10-08 (11:53 to 16:38 UTC), one Test Coverage run on a pull request failed. Nothing in the current rules would have kept that pull request out of the queue. ### Proposed solution Add `Test Coverage` to `requiredChecks` in `.github/review-policy.json`, and make the workflow safe to require: - Trigger `test-coverage.yaml` on `merge_group`. - Drop the path filter from its `pull_request` trigger and do the same check inside the job, the way Code Quality's build and typecheck jobs do. A required check that never reports would block docs-only pull requests, so the job has to start on every pull request and skip its steps when no coverage input changed. The `push` trigger keeps its path filter, so runs on main stay as they are. This is a change to the review policy, so it is T3 and needs an owner's decision before the pull request can merge. The change is ready on a branch and I'll open the pull request against this issue. ### What it costs - Every pull request starts a Test Coverage run. On a docs-only change it checks out, starts the Redis service and exits. - Every queue entry that touches packages runs the suite again on the merge group commit. I haven't measured that run. On pull requests the job averages about 8 minutes: about 2 when Turbo replays everything from cache, and 11 to 15 when a widely used package changed. - The queue waits on that run, so a merge that touches packages takes longer to land. ### Rollout 1. Merge the pull request. The workflow change takes effect, and the ruleset is unchanged. 2. A maintainer runs `node scripts/sync-review-policy.mjs --apply` to add the required check. 3. Open pull requests with no Test Coverage run wait on the new check until their next push. Step 2 is separate on purpose. If the merge queue run turns out to be too slow, we can hold off on requiring the check without reverting the workflow. ### Decision needed Should Test Coverage be a required check that also runs in the merge queue? If yes, an owner of the CI and policy area labels this issue `decision: accepted`.

+
+A VS Code extension that renders the assistant-ui `Thread` in a webview. +1. From the monorepo root, install and build the workspace packages:
+

+   pnpm install
+   pnpm turbo build --filter='with-vscode^...'
+   ```
+

+
+4. Run **AUI Test Bed: Open Component Gallery** to see the kit components in an editor tab.

+## Fetch bridge
+
+The webview reaches the extension host through `@assistant-ui/vscode`: `vscodeFetch` tunnels each request over `postMessage`, and `serveWebviewHost` in `src/webviews.ts` answers it with the routes in `src/routes.ts`. The fixtures play in the extension host, not in the webview.

+| --- | --- | --- |
+| `POST /api/chat` | `src/fixtures/route.ts`, an AI SDK UI message stream | `auiTest.runtime=ai-sdk`: `useChatRuntime` with `AssistantChatTransport({ fetch: vscodeFetch })` |
+| `GET /testbed/served-requests` | the request log in `src/routes.ts` | probes that check what the host served and whether `req.signal` fired |
+| `GET`, `PUT /testbed/color-theme` | `src/routes.ts`, reads and sets the user `workbench.colorTheme` | `theme-follows` |
+| `GET`, `PUT /testbed/open-external` | `src/open-external.ts`, the host's `openExternal` log and its stub switch | `external-link` |
+
+## Links and threads
+
+`serveWebviewHost` also serves the webview's host calls. `installLinkInterceptor()` in `webview/main.tsx` sends link clicks to its `openExternal`, which records each URL in `src/open-external.ts` and opens it with `vscode.env.openExternal`. +

+   import { SeededMessages } from "../runtime";

+       category: "content", // "chat" | "content" | "agents"

+
+### Add a rich fixture
+
+A rich fixture streams parts the core fixtures do not: `reasoning`, `source`, `file` (a `data:` URL), `data` (a named data part), and `tool-call` with a `toolName` a tool UI is registered for, with a `result` (answered by the host) and optionally `isError`. `FixtureStep` in `src/fixtures/types.ts` lists every step; both fixture routes play them.

+

+

issue.title: ci: report vitest coverage for changed packages
issue.body: ## Problem CI runs the tests of changed packages but never measures what they cover, so a PR can add untested code paths and nothing shows it. There is also no command to measure coverage locally. ## Change - `@vitest/coverage-v8` goes in the root devDependencies, next to `vitest`. Its peer is exact `vitest` 5.0.1, which is what the workspace already locks, and every workspace resolves the root install by walking up. The lockfile churn is the `vitest@5.0.1` peer suffix picking up the provider. - Every workspace whose tests run on vitest (48 of them) gets `"test:coverage": "vitest run --coverage --coverage.reporter=text --coverage.reporter=html --coverage.reporter=json-summary"`, with a matching `test:coverage` task in `turbo.json` that outputs `coverage/**`. The reporters are named in the script so that a root, filtered, single-package or CI run all write the `coverage-summary.json` that the summary reads. Vitest's defaults, and `packages/cli`'s own reporter list, don't include it. The `node --test` workspaces (`x-buildutils`, `apps/registry`) are left out. - The five package-level `turbo.json` files that override `test` get the same override for `test:coverage`. `metro`, `vue` and `svelte` test against their own `dist`, and `assistant-stream` and `apps/docs` pass `REDIS_*` through. - For `assistant-stream` and `cloud`, `test:coverage` covers the main vitest run only. The peer-version legs still run in the Test job. - `scripts/coverage-summary.mjs` reads each workspace's `coverage/coverage-summary.json` and renders a markdown table, one row per package plus a combined row weighted by size. `pnpm coverage:summary` prints it, and `--report ` writes it to a file instead; `-- --report ` and `--report=` work too. `pnpm test:coverage` runs coverage across the repo and passes turbo flags through, so `pnpm test:coverage --filter=@assistant-ui/core` works. A filtered run leaves other packages' earlier reports in place, and the summary includes them. - A new Coverage job in Code Quality picks packages the same way the Test job does, with the same Redis service and `--concurrency=1`. It writes the table to the job summary and uploads the HTML and JSON reports as a `coverage` artifact kept for 14 days. The job only reports. It sets no threshold and posts no PR comment. Both can follow once the numbers have settled, and the size report's sticky-comment step is the pattern for a comment. The Coverage job reruns the changed packages' tests alongside the Test job. That adds runner minutes but not wall time. Folding coverage into the Test job instead would mean running the `assistant-stream` and `cloud` peer legs separately. ## Verification - `pnpm coverage:test`: 6 `node --test` cases pass. Two run the script as a subprocess, covering all three `--report` forms and a missing path. - By hand: `pnpm test:coverage --filter=@assistant-ui/tap --filter=assistant-ui`, `pnpm -C packages/store test:coverage`, `pnpm coverage:summary`, and `pnpm coverage:summary --report ` against `pnpm run coverage:summary -- --report `, which produce identical files. - `pnpm turbo test:coverage --concurrency=1 --continue -- --coverage.reporter=json-summary` across the whole repo, run locally: all 48 packages report. Combined coverage is 87.5% lines, 85.6% statements, 82.2% functions and 78.6% branches. Redis wasn't running, so `assistant-stream`'s Redis suites skipped and its 89.6% lines is low. - The first full run failed `metro` because `test:coverage` lacked its `build` dependency. After the override, `metro`, `vue` and `svelte` pass. - `pnpm lint` passes, and the workflow YAML parses. The Coverage job has not run in CI until this PR. ## Public surface None. The published packages change only in `scripts` entries, which need no changeset. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

issue.title: rsky-relay: listHosts/getHostStatus return JSON as Content-Type: text/plain
issue.body:
**Describe the bug**

`com.atproto.sync.listHosts` and `com.atproto.sync.getHostStatus` return valid JSON with `Content-Type: text/plain; charset=utf-8`. Both lexicons declare `"encoding": "application/json"` for output. `/_health` is correct (`application/json`).


The cause is [`write_response` in `rsky-relay/src/server/server.rs`](https://github.com/blacksky-algorithms/rsky/blob/aec5598939fa3df724c313b101935c8210536ece/rsky-relay/src/server/server.rs#L202-L208
), which hardcodes `text/plain; charset=utf-8`.


The listHosts and getHostStatus arms pass it `serde_json::to_string(...)` output. On `fix/relay-throughput-parity`, commit 035324e4 added `write_json`, but [only the `/_health` arm uses it](https://github.com/blacksky-algorithms/rsky/blob/aec5598939fa3df724c313b101935c8210536ece/rsky-relay/src/server/server.rs#L400-L432
).

**To Reproduce**

Steps to reproduce the behavior:

1. `curl -sI "https://atproto.africa/xrpc/com.atproto.sync.listHosts?limit=1" | grep -i content-type`
  1. Output: `content-type: text/plain; charset=utf-8`
1. `getHostStatus` gives the same result for both 200 and 400 responses, e.g. `curl -sI "https://atproto.africa/xrpc/com.atproto.sync.getHostStatus?hostname=bsky.network"`
  1. Output: `content-type: text/plain; charset=utf-8` 

Compare both to `curl -sI https://atproto.africa/_health`, which returns `content-type: application/json`

**Expected behavior**

Responses with JSON bodies should use `Content-Type: application/json`, as the lexicons declare.

**Details**

- Operating system: N/A
- Node version: N/A

Encountered this while building an app that monitors uptime across the ecosystem and had to build an exception. Figured it'd be kind to report the issue.
